policy_notes.shared_conversions: R3: one confidence label in guidance.py used by architecture guidance and reassessment, one bounded free-text list reader, one confidence clamp, one group-parent reader, one persistence digest, and one strength band. policy_notes.semantic_job_port: R4: the semantic persistence port stops publishing a member none of its thirteen consumers used, and stops publishing a private snapshot resolver that application modules were reaching into. policy_notes.caller_obligations: R5: the maintenance-task assessment records what a caller must know or guarantee because the interface does not enforce it. Optional field, so assessments saved before it stay valid and no repository re-map is forced: it lives in the response schema, and semantic_input_hash is byte-identical before and after. Adds 18 production lines; no new endpoint, service, dependency, model stage, or aggregate quality score. Acceptance: tests/test_caller_obligations.py.
policy_notes.scoped_domain_meaning: R6: a Charter claim may name the area that owns a rule, and the Charter may record terms whose meaning is scoped, including the other scopes that use the same word for a different thing. Both optional, so charters saved before them stay valid; semantic_input_hash is byte-identical so no re-synthesis is forced. A principal can declare a scoped meaning through the existing correction path rather than have one inferred from names. Adds 42 production lines; no new endpoint, service, table, or model stage. Acceptance: tests/test_domain_definitions.py.
policy_notes.attributed_verification: R8: a recommendation may carry an optional bounded transformation (exact target, preconditions, a short ordered sequence, the preserved behavior, a verification command and a rollback) plus an optional result whose status is unverified unless a tool that actually ran the check supplied it and named the revision it ran on. AnaxiGraph never runs the change, so a result that does not name its revision is not evidence about the reviewed revision and is reported as unchecked on the grounded item and in the dashboard. Both blocks are optional, so reviews saved before them stay valid; semantic_input_hash is byte-identical so no re-review is forced. Net 46 production lines after removing 45 lines of duplication in the same commit: one AST naming helper instead of two, one snapshot-replay algorithm instead of two, one priority and rule-attention vocabulary in the foundation layer instead of one per layer, one snapshot metadata reader, one CLI database default, and an unused instruction helper deleted. No new endpoint, service, table, dependency or model stage. Acceptance: tests/test_transformation_verification.py.
policy_notes.scan_recovery: 0.7.1: the optional contract fields added in 0.7.0 are absent from each object's required list, which strict structured output forbids, so the Codex adapter now builds a nullable wire schema without touching the stored contract and translates those nulls back to absence before validation. Charter reduction takes its sections from the schema instead of a list kept beside it, which is what silently dropped scoped definitions. Authorising a retry moves the ceiling by one rather than zeroing the attempt count, so a repeatedly authorised failure stays visible. Net negative by one production line. Acceptance: tests/test_codex_schema.py, tests/test_semantic_failure_telemetry.py, tests/test_scan_recovery_contracts.py.
policy_notes.stage_models: 0.7.2: a repository may name a model per kind of work, so routine file descriptions run on a cheaper model than the repository Charter. The tier is read from the request the planner already builds, so no planner or worker protocol changed. The model that produced a document travels with the result and is what provenance records, because a staged run claims with the run default and may execute on another model; recording the claim would misname the author of every synthesis. semantic_stage_model.py is a new foundation module holding the tier names, their parser and the request-to-tier rule. That gives anaxigraph.config a fan-out of one, its first: config.py was over the 500-line ceiling with no seam its own checker could find, and the concept has two consumers rather than being a split made to satisfy a line count. Two legacy function exceptions were retired in the same change because extracting _choice and _spending brought _semantic_config back within normal policy. Acceptance: tests/test_stage_models.py. A tier also names its executor, because which command-line tool runs is part of choosing a model: a run launched against Codex cannot reach a Claude model otherwise. The executor that ran a job travels with the result alongside the model, so a mixed run does not record every document as written by the tool that happened to claim it. --stage-model sets a tier for one run without editing the policy, since the cost is felt at the run.
policy_notes.findings_page_cost: 0.7.2: ranking a finding no longer writes its prose. A repository with 61,636 findings took over a minute to return a page of five because plain_language_contract ran for every row before filtering and paging, and almost all of it was discarded. Score, reasons and actionability stay on every row because ranking, the architecture_area filter and diagnostic grouping all read them; the sentences are written for the returned page only, before the byte budget is measured. Measured on 61,636 synthetic findings: 29.7s to 1.6s. The live figure is not claimed here because the live service runs an older build. Acceptance: tests/test_finding_page_cost.py.
policy_notes.skipped_stage_reporting: 0.7.2: a skipped stage reads as skipped. Pattern review is off by default, and status reported patterns.ready true while patterns.enabled was false, concluded that the map was up to date, and omitted the stage from compact status entirely, so a reader saw full coverage, no pattern findings, and no reason why. The internal gate is unchanged: _patterns_ready still answers whether the stage blocks baseline_complete, and a disabled stage does not block it. Only the reported readiness, the conclusion sentence and the compact payload changed. Acceptance: tests/test_pattern_stage_reporting.py.
policy_notes.dispatch_family_signal: Adds a deterministic Python analyzer fact, dispatch_family: a family of >=2 sibling or elif branches comparing the same expression to different string literals, each doing something different (not a membership validation check, which compares with in, not ==). Referenced as an additional problem_signal on provider-abstraction, bridge, decorator and strategy, so a candidate can be selected before any inheritance exists, at the moment a branch family is actually growing, rather than only after classes were already built. Threshold (count_gte 3) calibrated against a whole-repository scan: families of size 2 are common (10 in this repository) and mostly unremarkable; size >=4 is rare (6) and each occurrence is worth a look. This raises candidacy, not a verdict: the existing semantic_questions step still judges whether branches are genuinely interchangeable behavior or merely share a variable name. No JS/TS equivalent yet. Net +72 production lines, no offsetting deletion found. Acceptance: tests/test_analyzers.py.
policy_notes.interactive_workflows: User-requested interactive mapping, pattern-analysis and fresh-eyes diagrams with saved coverage, model provenance, reuse, live progress and explicit run/resume controls. Reuses existing queues, planners and worker coordination; adds two REST endpoints, two Python modules and four dashboard assets, with no dependency, database schema, MCP tool or default-model change. Local regression evidence: 89 Python tests and 35 browser tests pass; these are fixture runs, not model-quality benchmarks. The authorized feature sets the measured source baseline from 65021 to 65993 lines; all existing function, module and dependency limits remain enforced.

policy_notes.illustrated_workflow_frontend: User-requested correction to match the mapping SVG in the actual dashboard: Workflows becomes the opening screen and a primary navigation item; each flow has a direct URL, the illustration palette, recorded-model legend and explicit evidence arrows. policy_notes.workflow_sqlite_contention: User-requested repair of step 3 stopping under 16 workers with OperationalError: database is locked. Module search refreshes now hydrate only selected file facts and symbols, and request evidence reads paths without expanding unrelated metadata. SQLite write admission retries only SQLITE_BUSY within a bounded deadline; the transaction body and provider call are never replayed. Heartbeats use the same transaction path and calculate expiry after acquiring the lock. Acceptance: a 96-file context workflow with 16 workers drains six waves despite deliberately contended saves, with one provider call and one attempt per file; claim, heartbeat, bounded-wait, rollback and incremental-search regression tests exercise real SQLite connections. No model, endpoint, schema, dependency or concurrency-limit change. The exact source baseline moves from 67049 to 67081 for this repair; existing function, module and coupling limits remain enforced.

Supported provider-specific model dropdowns and server validation prevent invented or mismatched model IDs; saved Claude family names migrate to exact supported versions. Parallel model pools share an atomically leased queue, isolate executor-wide rejection, continue per-file failures and honor durable retry backoff and attempt ceilings. Retry errors and unavailable pools appear on cards. Acceptance: 96-file, 16+16-worker fixture runs complete with both models and with one rejected provider; all-provider rejection stops after the initial calls and retains pending work. Focused tests cover temporary and permanent file failures, exact sample limits, pinned reviews, settings migration and browser controls. Model catalogs were checked without inference; these workload figures use simulated providers. The source baseline moves from 67081 to 67240 for this repair; no function, module, coupling or CI gate is relaxed.

policy_notes.workflow_saved_progress: User-requested repair for source scans making saved workflow work appear never run, and for unnecessary proposal regeneration after small changes. No live model jobs are launched. The exact production baseline moves from 67506 to 67837 lines; the review-planning function baseline is lowered to 62 lines and complexity 4. Existing size, coupling and complexity limits remain enforced. Workflow view transitions no longer move viewport-fixed loading feedback or its retry control. Counts remain visible while a new scan awaits reuse planning, without treating earlier results as current.
policy_notes.execution_continuity_audit: User-requested audit and repair of hidden execution cutoffs. Full CLI runs drain by default; explicit samples remain bounded. Providers are simulated; no live model run is launched. Exact production baseline moves from 67899 to 68203 lines for these requested repairs. No module, function, coupling or CI limit is relaxed.
policy_notes.workflow_prerequisite_execution: User-requested faster preparation, concurrent step requests and automatic prerequisite updates. Requests share per-card pools and the repository worker ceiling; duplicate requests coalesce. Progress distinguishes preparation, real active workers, waits and completion checks, and re-reads across coordinator transitions. Acceptance: real SQLite workflow tests cover overlap, pool limits, single claims, reuse after source changes, optional review contracts and idempotent index installation; browser contracts cover simultaneous cards, prerequisites, completion, configuration and saved progress. Providers are simulated; no live mapping is launched. Existing saved-progress JavaScript functions are decomposed to resolve CI self-analysis findings. Exact production baseline moves from 68203 to 68374; existing function, module, coupling and CI limits remain enforced.

The measured production baseline changes from 68374 to 68932 lines for this explicitly requested increment. No new service, database table, endpoint, MCP tool, dependency or CI gate. Model output quality and delivery improvements remain unmeasured. policy_notes.compact_guidance_preservation_2026_10_20: Follow-up to the requested small-output and useful-core items: preserve every selected implementation path and compact verification/placement references, while tests stay in the relevant-tests collection. A final fallback shortens duplicate prose when a repository explicitly selects a 4 KB budget. Reuse the agent-response formatter for compact findings. policy_notes.portable_architecture_planning: User-authorized architecture planning and repository-carried analysis: optional agent-selected options and target diagrams extend the existing semantic queue; deterministic checksummed logical records rebuild the local SQLite cache after a normal Git pull. Acceptance uses real Git round trips with full AI results, zero-call reuse, corruption, dirty sources, partial/interrupted publication and no-op saves. Exact production baseline: 72405. Function, module and default coupling caps remain unchanged. Config adds one dependency on the shared foundation record recognizer so malformed or unrelated record.json files cannot hide source or break loading. Its existing high-fan-in exception records fan-out two rather than duplicating recognition. New modules obey normal caps.
policy_notes.current_checkout_storage: User-authorized correctness repair of a reported 3.22 GB failed all-history export. Configuration gains one storage policy; existing canonical temporal readers gain direct consumers for current export/import and checkpoint-preserving pruning. Their exact fan-in counts are recorded, their fan-out stays bounded, and no general function/module/complexity/layer ceiling is raised. The demonstrated storage-corruption/growth repair is the intentional production-source exception; the measured source baseline changes from 72405 to 73885 (+1480 lines). Acceptance: 32 focused current-storage, migration-command, portable-record and cross-index review tests pass; real application-source mapping uses about 22 MB locally.
